mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep improving from their current depressed levels, weekday trip generation will rise first and then feed into retail visits, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase from their current levels.

mechanism_narrative: A further drop in RESIDENTIAL time below the current elevated baseline signals more time spent outside home, which should translate into more discretionary retail visits within one to two weeks and a higher RETAIL_REC mean over the next month.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 9.0% for two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL dropping below the stated threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both suppressed, retail demand is constrained by commuting and office-linked purchases; if these two series stay near the current negative band, RETAIL_REC will remain lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay at or below their current weak levels.

mechanism_narrative: An upswing in PARKS mobility relative to its recent trough indicates recovered discretionary movement, and that same rebound should spill into nearby retail and recreation visits within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in the following week after PARKS posts a week-on-week increase of 5 points or more.

mechanism_narrative: If grocery trips keep absorbing essential demand while transit remains weak, consumers will postpone discretionary shopping and RETAIL_REC will stay below the prior four-week average over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated relative to retail and TRANSIT remains depressed.

mechanism_narrative: A short-lived rebound in PARKS combined with stable RESIDENTIAL time implies more out-of-home leisure without a broad mobility recovery, which should push retail visits up over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above -50 while RESIDENTIAL stays between 8 and 10
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 14 days when PARKS and RESIDENTIAL meet the stated joint condition.

mechanism_narrative: A winter-season decline in PARKS mobility and a concurrent stabilization of TRANSIT imply movement is shifting indoors rather than expanding overall, which should limit retail recovery over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even though PARKS weakens further and TRANSIT does not recover.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES continues edging up while RESIDENTIAL declines from its current plateau, the implied easing of stay-at-home behavior should raise discretionary shopping demand, with the effect appearing over a four-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -28 and RESIDENTIAL falls below 9.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below its prior four-week mean over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL crossing the stated thresholds.
